extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of gasoline distribution and bulk gasoline terminal facilities; environmental compliance officers; state delegated authorities; environmental lawyers and permit writers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and final-rule revisions to NESHAP Subpart R, NESHAP Subpart BBBBBB, and NSPS Subpart XXa addressing definitions, monitoring and testing procedures, recordkeeping, tables of applicability, compliance dates, and associated economic/environmental analyses for gasoline distribution and bulk gasoline terminals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of “thermal oxidation system” and related terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalize revisions to the definitions of “flare” and “thermal oxidation system” as proposed; retain the historically used description of “thermal oxidation system” rather than replace with “vapor combustion unit.” Delete the phrase “other than a flare” where it occurred in references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA opted not to change the long-used description of the system to avoid inconsistencies with permits and ancillary requirements; flares are not a subset of thermal oxidation systems based on the final definitions. The final text deletes ‘other than a flare’ from multiple references (e.g., 40 CFR 63.427(a)(3), 63.11092(b)(1)(iii), item 1 of table 3 to NESHAP subpart BBBBBB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise references from 'thermal oxidation system other than a flare' to 'thermal oxidation system'
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace instances of the phrase “thermal oxidation system other than a flare” with simply “thermal oxidation system.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This revision reflects the final definitions where flares are not a subset of thermal oxidation systems and avoids implying a hierarchical relationship that does not exist under the final definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1 to Subpart R — 40 CFR 63.9(f) applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Set the entry for 40 CFR 63.9(f) in table 1 to Subpart R to “no.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 63.9(f) is a notification for conducting visible emission observations; there is not a requirement in NESHAP subpart R to conduct routine visible emission observations, so the table entry is updated to reflect non-applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 4 to Subpart BBBBBB — 40 CFR 63.7(e)(3) exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise the entry for 40 CFR 63.7(e)(3) in table 4 to subpart BBBBBB to include an exception for 40 CFR 63.11092(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The performance test requirements in NSPS subpart XXa, referenced in NESHAP subpart BBBBBB, specify test run duration; table entries are aligned to reflect that linkage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct cross-reference 40 CFR 63.10(b)(2)(ii)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise the entry for 40 CFR 63.10(b)(2)(ii) in table 4 to subpart BBBBBB to correct the cross-reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an editorial/cross-reference correction to ensure the table points to the correct regulatory paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of alternative work practice equipment leak provisions (40 CFR 63.11(c)-(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise the entry for 40 CFR 63.11(c) through (e) in table 4 to subpart BBBBBB to “yes, except . . .” and add a similar comment to table 1 to subpart R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The equipment leak alternative work practice may apply for some facilities (particularly co-located gasoline terminals) in lieu of monthly AVO monitoring, but it is not applicable to Method 21 monitoring associated with performance testing and is not applicable upon compliance with the instrument monitoring equipment leak provisions in 40 CFR 63.11089(c) (and similarly 63.424(c) for subpart R).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of flare provisions note (40 CFR 63.11(a)-(b), table notes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise the note for the 40 CFR 63.11(b) entry in table 4 to subpart BBBBBB by replacing “until compliance” with “except these provisions no longer apply for flares used to comply” and change “Item 2.b” to “Item 2.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that the exception applies for flares complying with flare provisions in NSPS subpart XXa, which are referenced in NESHAP subpart BBBBBB; also corrects cross-reference errors (update in table 1 to subpart R note to reference §§ 63.422(b)(2) and 63.425(d)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial corrections and consistency edits
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalize proposed editorial and typographical corrections; spell out acronyms at first use or replace words with acronyms; consistently refer to “liquid product” loaded into “gasoline cargo tanks”; make conforming revisions between the three rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes fixing typos (e.g., change “specifices” to “specifies”), correcting cross-references, and harmonizing phrasing across NESHAP subpart R, NESHAP subpart BBBBBB, and NSPS subpart XXa.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 63.422(a)(2) — 'affected facility' terminology and vapor-tight cargo tank meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise the term “affected facility” to “gasoline loading rack affected facility” and add a sentence clarifying that the definition of “vapor-tight gasoline cargo tanks” in §63.421 applies to the cross-referenced provisions in NSPS subpart XXa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies scope and ensures the cross-referenced term carries the intended meaning within subpart R and across linked NSPS provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 63.422(c)(1) punctuation to clarify alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Add “or” after the semicolon in 40 CFR 63.422(c)(1) to clarify that the provisions in this paragraph are alternatives to those in 63.422(c)(2) and (3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple editorial change to remove confusion regarding whether listed items are alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 63.425(d) — clarify annual LEL monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Add phrase “. . . and, if applicable, the provisions in paragraph (j) of this section” to clarify that annual LEL monitoring must also be conducted for internal floating roof storage vessels in addition to the requirements in 40 CFR 60.113b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that annual LEL monitoring applies where appropriate to internal floating roof storage vessels.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 63.425(e)(1) — table redesignation
rubrics_metrics.description: Redesignate the table at 40 CFR 63.425(e)(1) as table 1 to paragraph (e)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial renumbering for clarity because it is the first table in the section immediately following paragraph (e)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 63.425(f) — remove incorrect Method 21 reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Delete the phrase “except omit section 4.3.2 of Method 21” because Method 21 does not contain section 4.3.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrects an erroneous instruction referencing a non-existent section of Method 21.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 63.425(g)(3) — revise 'N' definition cross-reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise the definition of the term “N” to refer to the fourth column of table 1 to paragraph (e)(1) because a column was added and the cross-reference was not updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures the numeric symbol 'N' points to the intended table column after table modification.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 63.427(d) — operation consistent with operating parameters; deviations defined
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise 40 CFR 63.427(d) to indicate the vapor processing system should be operated in a manner consistent with the minimum and/or maximum operating parameter value or required procedures; operation constituting excess emission or failure to perform required procedures is a deviation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that normal operation should stay within specified parameter limits and sets forth when operation constitutes a deviation of the emissions standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 63.428(c)-(d) — recordkeeping clarifications and new paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify that recordkeeping requirements in paragraph (c) are for bulk gasoline terminals subject to 63.422(b)(1); add a new paragraph (d) providing recordkeeping requirements specific to 63.422(b)(2) (updated monitoring requirements for thermal oxidation systems, vapor recovery systems, and flares).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separates and clarifies recordkeeping responsibilities for sites under expiring/current requirements versus those subject to updated monitoring requirements aligned with NSPS subpart XXa.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 63.428(h) — terminology change to 'delegated authority'
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace the phrase “delegated air agency” with “delegated authority.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminology update for consistency with other rule language and delegation frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 63.428(l)(2)(ii) — clarify referenced periodic reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify that the periodic reports referenced are those required as specified in 40 CFR 60.115b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixes a cross-reference so regulated parties know which periodic report requirements apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 63.11083(c) — 3-year compliance schedule applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Add “. . . § 63.11086(a) or in . . .” after “as specified in” to note the 3-year compliance schedule also applies to bulk gasoline plants with an increase in daily throughput that exceeds the 4,000 gallons per day threshold for vapor balancing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures that facilities becoming subject to the rule through throughput increases receive the same 3-year compliance schedule available to other affected facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 63.11092(i) — align performance test conduct with Subpart R
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise 40 CFR 63.11092(i) to align the conduct of performance tests with requirements in NESHAP subpart R and clarify how performance tests should be conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harmonizes test procedures and expectations between subparts R and BBBBBB to reduce inconsistencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 63.11094 — records retention and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify that records must be maintained for at least 5 years unless otherwise specified and that electronic records are acceptable and should be made available for review at the time of inspection or provided to the inspector within a mutually agreeable timeframe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA is not requiring hardcopies; owners/operators may use hardcopy records but electronic records are sufficient; inspectors should be able to view electronic records during inspection and be provided copies as requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 63.11094 renumbering and addition of missing paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Renumber proposed paragraphs to ensure sequential order and add missing recordkeeping requirements (f)(5) through (7) that were intended to specify recordkeeping for facilities using different control technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added recordkeeping requirements are similar to those in NSPS subpart XXa and match reporting requirements included in the NESHAP subpart BBBBBB proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 60.501a — remove duplicative 'flare' definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Delete the duplicative definition of “flare” that was inadvertently included at the end of the definition of “equipment.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes accidental duplication in the NSPS subpart XXa definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 60.502a(b)-(c) — clarify performance test timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Add “. . . no later than the date on which § 60.8(a) requires a performance test to be completed” to clarify that full compliance cannot be assessed until the required performance test or evaluation is conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges that compliance determinations rely on required testing timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 60.502a(c)(3) — applicability to thermal oxidation systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Add language to 60.502a(c)(3) stating that the paragraph applies “or if a thermal oxidation system for which these provisions are specified as a monitoring alternative is used” so the provisions can apply to certain thermal oxidation systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This addition recognizes expanded use of flare monitoring provisions for certain thermal oxidation systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 60.502a(c)(3)(vi) — delete 'gasoline' qualifier; alternative election language
rubrics_metrics.description: Delete the word “gasoline” in reference to cargo tanks (flow rate is based on total liquid loading rates) and rephrase to clarify that “you may elect” to use this alternative to determine flare waste gas flow rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that the alternative can be used based on all cargo tank liquid loading, not just gasoline cargo tanks, and clarifies the elective nature of the alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 60.502a(h) — correct unit conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise “450 millimeters” to “460 millimeters” to correct the conversion from 18 inches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrects a unit conversion error in the NSPS text.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 60.503a(a)(1) — testing run requirement clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: Add the sentence: “The three-run requirement of § 60.8(f) does not apply to this subpart.” to clarify that only one 6-hour test as described in 60.503a(c) must be conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that the general three-run requirement in § 60.8(f) is not required for this subpart; one prescribed multi-hour test suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 60.503a(a)(2) — scope of pre-performance test leak monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace wording so that pre-performance test leak monitoring must include equipment, including loading arms, in the gasoline loading rack affected facility (not just potential sources in the terminal's vapor collection system equipment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires that pre-test leak monitoring include all relevant equipment at the gasoline loading rack affected facility, including loading arms and vapor processing system components.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 60.505a(a)(6) — leak recordkeeping requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a requirement to maintain records for leaks identified under 60.503a(a)(2), similar to records maintained for leaks identified under 60.502a(j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures documentation is kept for identified leaks discovered during pre-test monitoring with retention consistent with other leak recordkeeping provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 40 CFR 60.505a(c)(6)(ii) — remove redundant reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove a redundant reference to 60.502a(j)(2) in the applicability language because 60.505a(c)(6)(ii) already limits applicability to leaks identified using AVO during normal activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cleans up redundant citation to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and compliance dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective date for the final rule requirements (NESHAP Subpart R, NESHAP Subpart BBBBBB, NSPS Subpart XXa) is July 8, 2024. Compliance date for existing gasoline distribution facilities subject to NESHAP subpart R and BBBBBB is May 10, 2027, with specified exceptions; new sources must comply upon the effective date or upon startup, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions to the May 10, 2027 compliance date include changes to certain table entries, removal of SSM exemptions (which must be complied with by the effective date), finalized external floating roof fitting controls timing, and performance test reporting deadlines. EPA considered 3 years after promulgation as as-expeditious-as-practicable for compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for installation of fitting controls on external floating roof storage vessels
rubrics_metrics.description: Require installation of fitting controls the next time the storage vessel is completely emptied and degassed or 10 years after promulgation of the final rule, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligning installation of controls with planned degassing events minimizes offsetting emissions that occur during degassing; this timing may reduce implementation burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance test and performance evaluation reporting deadline (40 CFR 63.9(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: Require that reporting requirements for performance tests and performance evaluations be submitted following procedures in 40 CFR 63.9(k) 180 days after the promulgation date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the timing and procedures for required reports tied to performance testing and evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: RIA and economic/benefit/cost analyses required and summarized
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA prepared and summarized Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA) materials: estimates of affected facilities (~9,500 total; ~210 major; ~9,260 area), emissions baseline and reductions (HAP and VOC reductions by rule), total capital costs and annualized cost impacts, small-entity impact analysis, a partial equilibrium model of the U.S. gasoline market projecting negligible price/quantity changes, and monetized ozone-related health benefits using 3% and 7% discount rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RIA and supporting documents are available in the docket; analyses include PV and EAV benefit estimates by subpart, estimates of secondary emissions (e.g., CO2, NOx), and a conservative small-business impact assessment with metrics expressed as percent of revenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental justice (EJ) analysis and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA defines EJ as “the just treatment and meaningful involvement of all people, regardless of income, race, color, national origin, Tribal affiliation, or disability, in agency decision-making...”; EPA will consider EJ concerns and ways to protect communities bearing unequal environmental burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA includes an EJ discussion in the preamble and RIA, recognizing disproportionate burdens and continuing to consider protective measures for affected communities.
